items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: I had the chance to, actually I shared a floor with Milt Hinton for a few months.

ctx.x: Absolutely. You know great music changes the way we can feel about ourselves and about the world. And great musicians can do that. And those are the kind of people —

like being around people like Benny Carter and Joe Wilder, and I had the chance to, actually I shared a floor with Milt Hinton for a few months. We both had our practice studios where the musicians union building is now in New York City. That was where A&R Studios was for many years. And on the fifth floor there was a radio network for the blind. And they had several vacant spaces and I shared a rehearsal room with a guy, and Milt’s room was right next door. And I got to see him a couple of times there. And he…

Well it seems like the business has changed pretty rapidly. Like you probably have an agent? You have a manager. In years past a guy like Milt Hinton probably would do his own booking. Are there advantages and/or disadvantages to the way things are now?
